snip.t: The first symptom of carbon monoxide poisoning is usually headache and general malaise, which occurs with carboxyhemoglobin concentrations around 10%.
| Carbon monoxide poisoning | Headache, cherry‑red skin, exposure to smoke/poor ventilation | Elevated carboxyhaemoglobin; improves with 100% O₂ |

Unreliable with: intense vasoconstriction or shock, movement, nail varnish, ambient light, jaundice, anaemia, carboxyhaemoglobin (reads falsely high in carbon monoxide poisoning) and methaemoglobinaemia (reads about 85%).

qs.q: Following carbon monoxide poisoning, a patient survives the acute phase but later develops delayed white matter demyelination. Which deep gray matter structure exhibits characteristic bilateral necrosis?
qs.e: Bilateral necrosis of the globus pallidus is a hallmark of carbon monoxide toxicity due to its high metabolic demand. Mammillary bodies are typically damaged in thiamine deficiency.
qs.s: Pathology of Demyelinating Diseases: MS, NMO, ADEM, CPM: MCQs

qs.q: A patient presents with acute carbon monoxide poisoning. Which characteristic brain lesion is most likely to be observed?
qs.e: Carbon monoxide poisoning characteristically causes bilateral globus pallidus necrosis. While other areas like cortical layers III/V and CA1 hippocampus are also selectively injured, bilateral globus pallidus necrosis is highlighted as characteristic.
qs.s: Pathology of Demyelinating Diseases: MS, NMO, ADEM, CPM: MCQs

qs.q: Carbon monoxide poisoning is confirmed by measuring ---
o: Partial pressure of oxygen in blood
qs.e: Carboxyhemoglobin measurement directly reflects carbon monoxide binding to hemoglobin.

qs.q: In carbon monoxide poisoning, pulse oximetry is unreliable because
o: Absorbs more infrared light than OxyHb
qs.e: Standard pulse oximeters are unable to differentiate between carboxyhemoglobin (COHb) and oxyhemoglobin (OxyHb), interpreting COHb as OxyHb. This leads to a falsely normal or elevated SpO₂ reading, masking the severity of CO poisoning. Co-oximetry is required for accurate diagnosis.
